examShortTricks: Trick 1: Two voices structure the story: the tourist sees postcard beauty; the Nepali guide sees poverty and suffering behind it — the double vision IS the theme.
Trick 2: The tourist's exoticising gaze is critiqued — she consumes misery as scenery; collect two lines where her insensitivity shows.
Trick 3: The Buddha's half-closed eyes (compassion) vs the sinking sun (fading hope) — unpack both title images for the symbolism marks.
practiceQuestions: Q. How do the two characters see Nepal differently? (3 marks) — tourist: aesthetic beauty; guide: real suffering behind the beauty.
Q. What do the title's two images symbolise? (2 marks) — compassionate detachment (Buddha's eyes) and hope's decline (sinking sun).
keyPoints: Contrast: tourist's aesthetic gaze vs the reality of poverty and disability in Nepal.
The smile of the Buddha statue overlooks suffering — irony of spiritual tourism.
